description: One saved version of the presentation. Its folder, `versions/<time>/`, is named by when it was saved, in UTC to the second with dots for colons, then a dash and four lowercase letters or digits drawn at random above every tail the presentation's versions of that second have, as `versions/2026-10-30T16.20.05Z-k3pz/`, so that two computers saving in the same second both keep theirs, and one computer's saves in one second keep the order it made them in. Where no tail is left above, as when one of them is `zzzz`, it is drawn at random from all tails, passing by any already taken. The folder's name holds the version's time and tells versions apart: two computers saving offline can give two versions the same number, and both are kept. Version history lists versions newest first, in the reverse order of their folders' names: by their time, and within one second by their tails. The folder holds copies of the presentation's two files as they were saved, `presentation.mdpoint` and `slides.md`, and this file. MarkdownPoint opens a version only from its presentation's Version history, and opens nothing under the presentation's `versions/`, a version's folder or any other, as a presentation of its own. A version names its theme by key and shows the theme as it is now. It uses the presentation's own media. Delete Theme refuses a theme a version uses, and Clean Up keeps a file one uses. While a version's folder lacks one of its three files or this file can't be read, as while a sync service brings it, no theme can be deleted and Clean Up deletes nothing.

markdownpoint.description: The format version, its major and minor in quotes: "1.0". MarkdownPoint 1.x opens any version 1.x file. A newer major needs a newer MarkdownPoint.

number.description: The number MarkdownPoint shows: one past the highest version's when it was saved, so a version saved after the newest is deleted takes its number again.

name.description: The name the author gave it, on one line, not empty, with no tab or other control character, or none when left out.
